GRAP Stage III curbs remain in force as the government steps up pollution-control measures in New Delhi on November 15, 22026 | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma
Delhi's air quality was recorded in the 'very poor' category on Sunday (November 15, 2026) morning, with an Air Quality Index of 350, according to the Sameer app.
Of the 54 monitoring stations, 47 recorded 'very poor' air quality, while seven were in the 'severe' category. IIT Delhi recorded the highest Air Quality Index (AQI) at 428, followed by ITO at 414.
Delhi recorded a minimum temperature of 18.6 degrees Celsius on Sunday (November 15), which was 5.1 degrees below the season's average, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The weather department has predicted a cloudy sky with light rain or drizzle, with the maximum temperature expected to reach 27 degrees Celsius.
According to the CPCB, an AQI between zero and 50 is considered 'good', 51 to 100 'satisfactory', 101 to 200 'moderate', 201 to 300 'poor', 301 to 400 'very poor', and 401 to 500 'severe'.
